newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key 182nd JGB yield rises by 0.1 percentage point.
newsitem.headline: Key 182nd JGB yield rises by 0.1 percentage point.

text.p: The yield of the key 10-year 182nd Japanese government bond rose by 0.1 percentage point from Thursday's close to 2.255 percent in late afternoon trade on Friday.
The sharp rise was triggered by news earlier on Friday that the Finance Ministry had ordered Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co to halt some of its operations.

Traders said sentiment was hurt by worries that Nissan Life may be forced to sell its assets, which include yen bonds, and concerns over possible bond sales from life insurers other than the troubled Nissan Life.
"Life insurers may have to sell JGBs to take a share of the burden to help Nissan Life," said a securities house dealer.
A Nippon Life official denied on Friday rumours that the life insurer had been selling bonds, including foreign bonds, actively over the past two or three days.
Traders said vague rumours about a possible rise in interest rates also led to selling of JGBs.

"I think dealers are worried that a rise in Japanese interest rates, aimed at preventing a further fall in the yen against the dollar, may be agreed upon at the upcoming Japan-U.S. bilateral talks," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
The key 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.265 percent as of 0618 GMT, up sharply from the previous day's close of 2.155 percent.
